Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and next steps.

Short answers: 
- Region pinning: yes — we support region pinning for request payloads, generated tokens/outputs, embeddings, and session KV. For your pilot we can pin to Singapore (ap-southeast-1).
- Logs & telemetry: application-level request logs (headers/payloads) can be restricted to the same region; aggregated telemetry and anonymized runtime metrics may be processed in the US for platform analytics unless you opt out.
- Backups: backups are by default replicated across two regions for durability; for customers with residency requirements we offer a non-replicated backup profile that keeps backups only in the pinned region.
- Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessors list. Any subprocessor that would access customer data is disclosed; the attached PDF marks which subprocessors may access telemetry vs. content.

We don’t have cross-region processing for user content under a pinning config except in documented emergency failover scenarios (manual trigger or automatic fallback when the APAC region is unavailable). In those failover scenarios traffic is routed to the nearest compatible region and we notify customers via Console and API webhooks.

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_202601.pdf (contains subprocessor roles and region notes).

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll open a DPA addendum draft for APAC pinning and send it to you by EOD.
- If FinScale requires an onshore-only processing guarantee with no failover outside APAC, we’ll need to route that through our Private/Dedicated offering — I can get pricing.
- I’ll loop in our contracts and compliance folks for SOC2 and the DPA addendum.

Can you confirm whether your legal team needs a hard "no cross-border processing under any circumstances" clause or whether a failover exception with notification is acceptable?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the subprocessors list and talked to Compliance. High-level:

- We can produce a DPA addendum that restricts processing and backups to the pinned region with an explicit emergency failover carve-out. Proposed failover language: "In the event of prolonged regional unavailability, Redwood may route processing to an alternative region for the minimum duration necessary to restore service, and will notify the customer within 24 hours and provide a post-incident report."

- Backups: Non-replicated backups can be offered on hosted for pilot customers for an additional fee and a limited retention SLA. Production-grade non-replicated backups with stronger durability guarantees should be scoped under Dedicated.

- Subprocessors: there's one analytics subprocessor in the US that receives anonymized telemetry (no customer content). That will be explicitly excluded from content access in the addendum. Any subprocessor that needs content access will be documented and require written approval.

I attached a first-pass DPA addendum draft (dpa_apac_addendum_draft.docx). Please review and flag product/infra items we need to confirm (backup replication toggle, console flag for pinning, webhook notifications).
